queries: Klarna Siemiatkowski clarifies replaced Salesforce Workday built in-house not LLM
SaaSpocalypse software stocks selloff 2026 Anthropic Claude Cowork plugins Salesforce SAP shares fall

sources_considered.why: Describes the 2026 SaaS stock selloff and investors' fear that AI coding could reproduce software tools.
The best-known 'replaced Salesforce' case, and the CEO's later clarification of what Klarna actually built.

receipt.public_excerpt: The index lost 25 percent of its value between January 12, when Anthropic introduced Claude Cowork, an agent designed for professional work, and February 23, when it showed signs of recovering.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms that software stocks moved sharply on the AI-replaces-SaaS story. That is the uncontested part of the sentence. It does not show why the story took hold.

receipt.public_excerpt: his company had completely replaced a content management system it previously paid for, Sanity, with a custom setup it built from scratch.

evidence_items.explanation: The example cited for the story is a small CMS replacement, not SAP, Salesforce or Office 365. That fits the speaker's point but cannot test it.

receipt.public_excerpt: So no, we did not replace SaaS with an LLM,. Storing CRM data in an LLM would have its limitations. But we developed an internal tech stack, using Neo4j and other things, to start bringing data/knowledge together.

evidence_items.explanation: Klarna dropped Salesforce and built an internal stack, but its CEO said it did not replace SaaS with an LLM and doubted other companies would follow. One partial case cannot test a hyperbolic 'nobody'.

unresolved_gaps: No measure exists for the claimed mechanism: that the story 'set in' because it affirmed a pro-AI bias.
'Nobody' has no threshold, and no dataset tracks how many companies replace whole enterprise suites with in-house builds.
